newsitem.title: USA: Chronology of Oklahoma City bombing.
newsitem.headline: Chronology of Oklahoma City bombing.

text.p: The following is a chronology of events in the bombing of the Oklahoma City federal building, which killed 168 people. The trial of chief suspect Timothy McVeigh began on Monday.

April 19, 1995 - Huge explosion destroys Alfred P. Murrah building in downtown Oklahoma City at 9:02 a.m. Less than 90 minutes later, Timothy McVeigh is stopped for driving with no license plate near Billings, Oklahoma, and jailed for carrying a concealed weapon. Official death toll on first day is 30.
April 20 - FBI releases sketches of two possible suspects dubbed John Doe No. 1 and No. 2; investigators conclude bomb was in a Ryder truck rented in Kansas. Death count at 52.

April 21 - Just before he is due to be released, McVeigh is recognised as a bombing suspect and turned over to FBI; he makes his first court appearance at federal prison in El Reno, Oklahoma. His former Army buddy Terry Nichols surrenders in Kansas and is held as material witnesses. Death toll 78.
April 23 - National day of mourning. President Bill Clinton attends emotional memorial service in Oklahoma City.
April 24 - McVeigh's two court-appointed attorneys ask to be removed from case. Death toll reaches 80.
May 4 - Search of Murrah building ends with death toll at 167, including 19 children and a nurse killed during rescue effort; toll later rises to 168 when man dies in hospital.
May 8 - Stephen Jones named as McVeigh's new attorney.
May 10 - Terry Nichols is charged in bombing.
May 12 - Michael Tigar appointed Terry Nichols' attorney.
May 24 - Bombed-out shell of Murrah building is destroyed in controlled explosion but most relatives and survivors say hopes that demolition would bring "closure" prove premature.
Aug. 9 - Michael Fortier, another Army buddy of McVeigh, agrees to testify against him in plea bargain deal that calls for pleading guilty to lesser charges.
Aug. 10 - McVeigh and Terry Nichols formally indicted for bombing. Fortier indicted separately for knowing of plan but concealing his knowledge from investigators.
Feb. 20, 1996 - U.S. District Court Judge Richard Matsch moves trial to Denver to ensure fair hearing. The move draws bitter criticism from survivors and relatives of victims.
April 5 - Clinton and his wife Hillary in Good Friday visit to Oklahoma City; Clinton lays wreath at site of bombing and pays tribute to city's unity and spirit of renewal.

April 18 - U.S. House of Representatives approves counter-terrorism bill in compromise deal rushed through ahead of first anniversary of bombing. It requires chemical "tagging" of plastic explosives so they can be traced, but expanded wiretap powers are stripped from original proposal.
April 19 - Thousands of mourners join tearful first anniversary ceremony and pay tribute to the 168 people killed. A moment of silence is observed across the United States.
April 24 - Clinton signs anti-terrorism bill into law.
June 26 - Judge Matsch rules victims and relatives can not sit in court during trial if they are to testify.
Oct. 25 - McVeigh and Nichols are handed major victory as Judge Matsch orders separate trials for the two men.
Nov. 15, 1996 - Judge Matsch sets March 31, 1997, as the start of McVeigh's trial.
Jan. 29, 1997 - Judge Matsch rules that victims of bombing will be able to view trial on closed-circuit telecast at federal facility in Oklahoma City.

Feb. 28 - Dallas Morning News reports McVeigh admitted planting the bomb to defence team. Jones accuses newspaper of stealing documents and later says the "confession" was ruse to prompt a reluctant witness to speak with the defence. Jones insists his client has not confessed.
March 11 - Playboy Magazine publishes an article similar to that which appeared in Dallas Morning News.
March 14 - McVeigh's lawyers ask for charges against him to be dismissed, or the trial delayed for a year because of published articles saying McVeigh admitted planting the bomb.
March 17 - Judge Matsch denies defence requests, and Jones later takes plea to federal court of appeals.
March 25 - Judge Matsch reverses an earlier ruling and says he will allow victims of the bombing to view the proceedings even if they plan to testify in any penalty phase of trial.

March 28 - A federal appeals court denies requests by McVeigh's defence to postpone trial on grounds of prejudicial pre-trial publicity and other issues. The ruling clears way for trial to start as scheduled on March 31.
March 31 - Trial begins with jury selection.
